title: Apple-Mustard Wet Rub for Pork
description: Freeze-dried apple becomes a smooth, mild mustard paste that dissolves into the cooking juices of covered pork or ribs.

ingredients.name: plain freeze-dried apple powder
ingredients.note: Grind plain freeze-dried apple slices and measure the powder after grinding.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Plain broth without a vegetable blend.

steps.title: Smooth the apple powder
steps.text: Sift {apple} into a small bowl until no tough flakes remain.

steps.title: Hydrate the paste
steps.text: Whisk {mustard} and {broth} into the blend. Let stand 3 minutes and stir again until spreadable.

steps.title: Portion before cooking
steps.text: Portion about a tablespoon of clean paste per serving. Spread it on lean pork just before a covered braise, or whisk it directly into the braising liquid. Discard any paste contacted by raw meat.

notes: Make ahead: Mix the paste a day ahead, or keep the apple and spices dry and add mustard and broth just before use. Refrigerate clean prepared paste for up to 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze clean, unused portions for up to 1 month; the hydrated apple softens smoothly on thawing. Fridge reheat: Stir the chilled, unused paste and add directly to a braise before cooking. It needs no separate reheating. Freezer reheat: Thaw covered in the refrigerator overnight, stir well and add to the cooking liquid before the braise. Option A uses mustard and ginger. For gentler Option B, use smooth unsweetened applesauce in place of the mustard and omit the ginger. Estimated nutrition per serving of the prepared condiment (1/2 of recipe): 15 kcal, 0.4 g protein, 2.9 g total carbohydrate, 0.3 g fat, 0.5 g fiber, 3 mg sodium. Includes the measured broth and sauce. Sodium varies with your broth.
